Heated fluid expands, becomes less dense, and rises; cooler, denser fluid sinks to replace it, establishing convection loop C.
Closing switches P, R, and T establishes a closed circuit exclusively for bulb Y, so only bulb Y glows.

Tornado speed $\approx 300\text{ km/h}$; Cyclone calm eye diameter $\approx 10-30\text{ km}$; Cloud wall region $\approx 150\text{ km}$; Cloud region wind speed $\approx 150-200\text{ km/h}$.
Safety switches and fuses must always be connected in series with the live wire (not neutral wire) to isolate appliances from high voltage when turned off.

questions.topic: Acids vs Bases in Daily Life
questions.explanation: Spinach juice (oxalic acid) and apple juice (malic acid) are acidic. Baking soda, bleaching powder, and detergents are basic.
Drying wet clothes is physical, desirable, and slow. Fruit ripening, plant growth, and burning candles involve irreversible chemical changes.
Cotton is soft and compressible; thermocol and wooden blocks have lower density than water and float; thermocol is opaque.
Diluting concentrated acid is violently exothermic. Always add acid slowly down the sides of the beaker into water with constant stirring; never add water into acid.
Breaking a glass tumbler alters physical shape without creating new chemical bonds; however, shattered fragments cannot be reassembled spontaneously (physical, irreversible).

$2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{MgO}$; $\text{MgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{Mg(OH)}_2$. Magnesium hydroxide is basic: turns red litmus blue, China rose green, methyl orange yellow, and leaves blue litmus unchanged.
Sodium bicarbonate: $\text{NaHCO}_3$; Acetic acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$; Aluminium chloride: $\text{AlCl}_3$; Sodium chloride: $\text{NaCl}$; Nitric acid: $\text{HNO}_3$.
Sieving separates different particle sizes; magnetic separation extracts magnetic component Q; water dissolves soluble P, leaving insoluble S on filter paper; evaporating filtrate yields P.
The pitcher plant carries out green photosynthesis (autotrophic) but supplements nitrogen by enzymatic digestion of trapped insects (heterotrophic).
Photosynthesis requires light, chlorophyll, water, and $\text{CO}_2$. Synthesized glucose is stored as starch/cellulose (cell wall), and oxygen is released as a byproduct.
X: Incisor (chisel-shaped cutting), Y: Molar (broad grinding crown with multiple cusps), Z: Canine (pointed tearing tooth).
Inhalation of air is a physical mechanical ventilation process belonging to the respiratory system, not nutrition.
Weaving interlaces two sets of yarns (warp and weft) at right angles. Mohair is high-lustre luxury wool shorn from Angora goats.
Correct structural and functional pairings: P-(iv), Q-(i), R-(ii), S-(iii).
P: Table sugar (energy-giving carbohydrate, water-soluble); Q: Butter (energy-giving lipid, water-insoluble); R: Carrot (protective food rich in Vitamin A and fibre).
Crimped wool fibres create millions of microscopic dead air pockets; air is a poor conductor of heat and prevents body heat dissipation.
Coir is a resilient, waterproof natural cellulose fibre stripped from the fibrous mesocarp husk of coconut (*Cocos nucifera*).
Tap root system (W) corresponds to reticulate venation (carrot, dicots). Fibrous root system (X) corresponds to parallel venation (grasses, monocots).
The atlanto-axial joint connecting the atlas vertebra and axis tooth in the neck is a pivot joint permitting rotation.
Vitamin A (spinach, pumpkin), Vitamin C (amla, citrus fruits), Vitamin K (green leafy vegetables, egg yolk).
Emperor penguins huddle in dense social clusters in sub-zero Antarctic blizzards to reduce exposed body surface area and conserve metabolic warmth.
Atmosphere: $78\% \text{ N}_2$, $21\% \text{ O}_2$, $0.04\% \text{ CO}_2$. Atmospheric dinitrogen cannot be directly absorbed by plants; symbiotic *Rhizobium* convert it to soluble nitrates.
Longitudinal ovary section labels: antipodal cells at chalazal pole, central diploid secondary nucleus, and haploid egg cell flanked by synergids at micropylar pole.
The depth of the groundwater table varies widely from place to place depending on rainfall, geological soil permeability, and vegetation cover.
Frogs respire cutaneously through moist skin underwater and via lungs on land. Crows, crocodiles, and marine dolphins respire via lungs. Fish (rohu, salmon) respire via gills.

Slope of displacement-time graph gives instantaneous velocity. Slope decreases from O to P, becomes zero, then increases from P to Q. If initial and final positions coincide, net displacement is zero, yielding average velocity $= 0$.

Test tube I: Single displacement $\text{Fe} + \text{CuSO}_4 \to \text{FeSO}_4 + \text{Cu}$. Test tube II: Neutralisation $\text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \to \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Test tube III: Iron oxidation forming hydrated iron oxide rust $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (basic metal oxide).

Eosinophils and basophils are polymorphonuclear granulocytes defending against parasitic infections and mediating allergic inflammatory responses. Erythrocytes (RBCs) lack nuclei and transport respiratory gases.

Mustard has complete bisexual flowers undergoing cross-pollination. Cucumber has unisexual male and female flowers. Yeast is a budding unicellular fungus. *Oxalis* produces cleistogamous complete flowers that self-pollinate without opening.

Penguins display countershading camouflage (white belly hides against sky from below, dark back hides against ocean depths from above). Supraorbital salt glands located above the orbits excrete excess sodium chloride from ingested seawater.
